metric: Distinct (query, rewrite) pairs, from 4,160 rewrites by 13 systems of TPC-H, DSB, Calcite and SQLStorm queries, that the authors' PostgreSQL run flagged equal, proved equivalent as result bags. Of the 2,674 flagged pairs, 191 are refuted by a replayed database and left out of the denominator (instance-label disagreements): 126 by the directed search added on 2026-11-11 (tools/witness_search.py), 65 by the earlier sources of databases. No pair leaves the denominator for another reason; over all flagged pairs the score reads 2152/2674.
correctness: 0 wrong: every proof is replayed on the prover's counterexample, KumoSQL's targeted databases, for TPC-H a generated scale-0.01 instance, and one second of the directed search; a difference counts only when DuckDB agrees with its optimizer off and, for order-sensitive queries, in three row orders
held_out: 443/529 proved, 0 wrong (a fifth of the queries, by hash, with all their rewrites)
caveats: Data downloaded at a pinned commit (no licence; not bundled). Flags come from one PostgreSQL instance, so a refuted pair is a label disagreement, not an error. Quoted upper-case identifiers are folded to lower case (the Calcite queries quote tables created in lower case) and FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY is read as LIMIT n. 2 pairs flagged both ways are not scored. Until 2026-11-10 no prover rule had been written for this eval; the baseline on that day, before the rules (main c384968, this harness): 1354/2608 proved, 0 wrong, held out 279/555. Eight rule modules were then written against the unknown development pairs (tailed_grouping_sets.py, tailed_outer_aggregates.py, wrapped_join_filters.py, closed_sources.py, listed_output_names.py, one_row_tails.py, string_spelling_rules.py, printed_spelling.py) with an interval-arithmetic reading in string_number_compare.py, so the development pairs are tuned on. The held-out fifth was not: its pairs were run for scoring only and never read one by one, and no proof was lost on either part. Earlier harness history: FETCH FIRST read as LIMIT (the 100 development pairs that use it, 81 flagged equal, went from 16/67 to 7/67 proved, 0 wrong, at the time) and a 30 s limit on replaying a TPC-H instance without the optimizer, both from development pairs. On 2026-11-11 seventeen more rule modules were written against the unknown DSB development pairs (docs/provers.md, shape rules for planner-written rewrites), a column the DSB queries name differently from the published DDL was mapped (customer.c_last_review_date_sk), and the directed search was built on the same development pairs; the held-out fifth was again run for scoring only. Before that batch (main 22fed36): 1659/2609 proved with 65 refuted. The directed search has a time budget (8 s for an unproved pair), so the refuted count can move by a few pairs between runs and machines; KUMOSQL_DIRECTED=0 turns it off. On 2026-11-12 about seventy more rule modules were written against the 329 unknown TPC-H, Calcite and SQLStorm development pairs (docs/provers.md, shape rules; the DSB batch of the day before had left them alone), again with the held-out fifth run for scoring only and never read one by one. With both batches: 2042/2487 proved (the DSB batch alone: 1827/2479, main 7ce683c; before either: 1659/2609), held out 409/529 (376/528 with the DSB batch alone), and no pair that either main proved is lost on the whole corpus. On 2026-11-18 the VeriEQL worker rules (about 35 modules, one group that a pair they touched and nothing proved runs without) were merged with main edb3ae3 (batches 4 and 5): 2081/2480 proved, held out 413/528 (413/529 on main). 24 more large DSB pairs reach the 60 second cap and count as timeout (18 to 42, one error); none is proved by either tree. Run again on 2026-11-19 on 873f667 (hardest-cases batches 8 and 9, Kumo_SQL_Prover PR 44, merged with main c97feeb), alone on 4 cores in 110 minutes: the same 2,081 proofs by count and the same 413 of 528 held out, 0 wrong, and pair by pair every proof of the runs on f6585e0 and on e203738. The recorded score stays main's run. In this run 195 are refuted, 344 unknown, and 54 reach the 60 second cap (50 timeouts, 4 deadline errors; 43 in main's run): batch 9 runs as a second stage after the prover as it was ends without a verdict, and on about ten large DSB pairs that stage crosses the cap; none of them is proved by either tree. With the batch on from the first attempt six DSB proofs ran past the cap (2,101 against 2,107 proofs over the whole corpus on e203738 and f6585e0); the two stages are the fix and all six prove in this run. 2026-11-20 (the twelfth and thirteenth hardest-cases batches, Kumo_SQL_Prover PR 51): whole run on f9940a3 with nothing else running: the same 2,081 proofs of the pairs flagged equal and the same 413 of 528 held out, 0 wrong, so the row stands. Twelve unknown pairs reach the 60 second cap now (two more stages run before a pair is given up). Four DSB pairs refuted in the recorded run came out unknown in this one; each is refuted on both trees when decided alone (the directed search is bounded by wall-clock time), so the 2,480 stands. One pair's deadline surfaced as an argument error of the solver's library; the harness now counts that as a timeout. 2026-11-21 (the fifteenth hardest-cases batch, Kumo_SQL_Prover PR 53): the row is now the whole run on ad089f6, with nothing else running: 2115/2480 proved, held out 434/528, 0 wrong. They come from three last steps of a proof (docs/provers.md): a shared ORDER BY .. LIMIT set aside, a LIMIT lifted above its joins, and counts over joined child tables read as one counted table per child. The steps were written against unproved development pairs, which are therefore tuned on; the held-out pairs were run for scoring only and never read. Every one of these proofs carries the stated assumption about rows tied at a cut; each was repeated alone and survived 40 seconds of the directed search.
